SUBJECT:  SUBSTANTIAL  AMENDMENTS  TO FISCAL  YEAR  2019-2020,  2020-2021,  2022-
2023,  2023-2024,  &  2024-2025  ANNUAL  ACTION  PLANS  FOR  THE  COMMUNITY
DEVELOPMENT  BLOCK  GRANT  (CDBG)  FUNDS.

PURPOSE:  To consider  the proposed  Substantial  Amendments  to the FY  2019-2020,  2020-2021,
2022-2023,  2023-2024,  & 2024-2025  Annual  Action  Plans to reprogram  $1,706,245  in CDBG  funds.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  It is recommended  that the Citizen  Advisory  Committee  consider
staff's  recornrnendation  to reprogram  CDBG  funds  and recommend  to the City  Council  approval  of
the proposed  Substantial  Amendments  to the FY 2019-2020,  2020-2021,  2022-2023,  2023-2024,  &
2024-2025  Annual  Action  Plans to reprogram  $1,706,245  in CDBG  funds.

ANALYSIS:  Per HUD  regulations,  the City  is required  to carry  out its Community  Development
Block  Grant  (CDBG)  program  in a timely  manner.  As required  by 24 CFR  570.902  of the CDBG
regulations,  HUD  reviews  the City  for compliance  with  these requirements  each May  2. As part of a
detailed  plan to correct  course,  staff propose  reprogramming  $1,706,245  of unused  CDBG  funds  from
various  Annual  Action  Plans to a construction-ready  Street  Improvement  Project  located  in eligible
CDBG  census tracts  and consolidate  all Comtnercial  Fagade  and Business  Sign Programs  funds  into
one Commercial  Fagade Program.

The Street  Improvement  Project  will  encompass  street improvements  within  CDBG  eligible  census
tract areas:

  *  Industrial  Avenue  from  Main  Street to Century  Borilevard.
  *  Frontage  Road from  Southern  Avenue  to Miller  Way
  *  Pinehurst  Avenue  from  Tweedy  Boulevard  to Southern  Avenue
  *  Hildreth  Avenue  from  Southern  Avenue  to Tweedy  Boulevard

Staff recommend  allocating  the available  CDBG  funds as follows:

Programs  funds  into one Commercial  Fagade Program.

Current  Status  of Commercial  Fayade  and Business  Sign  Program.

The Cornrnercial  Fagade Improvement  Program  provides  grants for the exterior  rehabilitation  of street-
facing  businesses  in the public  right-of-way.  Improvements  may include  new paint,  new windows,  and
code compliance  business  signs, etc.

The Commercial  Fagade Program  since FY 2019 to FY 2024 assisted  four businesses  in improving  the
aesthetic  aspects of their properties.  The total amount  expended  was $206,747.

BACKGROUND:  The City  of South  Gate has been a recipient  of CDBG  funds  annually  since the
enactment  of the Housing  and Community  Development  Act  of 1974.  The  City  is deemed  as an
"entitlement"  jurisdiction  because  it maintains  a population  above  50,000  and meets  certain  other
demographic  criteria.  CDBG  funding  can be used for a variety  of projects  and programs  primarily
benefiting  persons  of low-  and moderate-income.

SUBJECT:  FISCAL  YEAR  2025-2026  COMMUNITY  DEVELOPMENT  BLOCK  GRANT
(CDBG)  FUNDING

PURPOSE:  That the Citizen  Advisory  Committee  (CAC)  consider  eligible  funding  requests  for the
estimated  $1.2 million  in FY 2025-26  CDBG  funding.  The CAC  will  hear presentations  from  public
and non- public  services  applicants  on Wednesday,  February  26, 2025.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  It is recommended  that tlie Citizen  Advisory  Committee  consider
eligible  applications  and  recommend  to the  City  Council  CDBG  funding  allocations  for  Public
Services  and Non-Public  services  for FY 2025-26.

ANALYSIS:  During  the month  of October,  emails  were  sent to non-profit  organizations  and city
departments  and a legal  notice  of funding  availability  was published  on October  31, 2024,  to inform
prospective  applicants  of the availability  of CDBG  funds  for fiscal  year 2025-26.  Applications  were
made available  online  and via email.  Completed  applications  were accepted  in the City  Clerk's  office
up  until  the deadline  of November  25, 2024.
